subject: questions on how to implement simulateData()

messages.author: 373e56ec89625c50
messages.subject: questions on how to implement simulateData()
parts:
Hello! I have two questions related on how non-normality is induced through the simulateData() function.
 
Q1: Say I have the following, very simple model (true.mod in my example). When I use simulateData() I can specify certain level of skewness but let the kurtosis take any value like this:
 
true.mod <- 'x1 ~~ 0.5*x2
             x1 ~~ 0.5*x3
             x2 ~~ 0.5*x3'
datum <- simulateData(true.mod, sample.nobs=1000, skewness=c(3,3,3))


But if I try it the other way around (i,e, specify the kurtosis but let the skewness free), I get the following error:
 
datum <- simulateData(true.mod, sample.nobs=1000, kurtosis=c(3,3,3))
Error in ValeMaurelli1983(n = sample.nobs[g], COR = cov2cor(COV), skewness = skewness,  :
  skewness has wrong length

Why does this happen? Is this because of how the Vale&Maurelli1983 method works? Is there anyway to specify the kurtosis but let the skewness be freely estimated in lavaan?
 
Q2: (this will use the psych package just for the describe() function). While I was playing around with some toy simulation examples, I wanted to see how accurately does simulateData() matches the values I give it for skewness/kurtosis (so the skewness/kurtosis parameters in the population). If I run a small simulation like this:
 
#true model
true.mod <- 'x1 ~~ 0.5*x2
             x1 ~~ 0.5*x3
             x2 ~~ 0.5*x3'

#number of simulation repetitions
reps <- 1000

#vectors to store the results
x1s <- double(reps)
x2s <- double(reps)
x3s <- double(reps)

#simulation loop
for (i in 1:reps) {
datum <- simulateData(true.mod, sample.nobs=1000, skewness=c(3,3,3))

x1s[i] <- describe(datum)$skew[1]
x2s[i] <- describe(datum)$skew[2]
x3s[i] <- describe(datum)$skew[3]
}

#they should be close to 3
> mean(x1s)
[1] 2.920994
> mean(x2s)
[1] 2.9537
> mean(x3s)
[1] 2.91432

I can see it recovers the population values quite nicely. Not too surprising, of course, since it's sample size of 1000 with 1000 repetitions (I'm sure for other people running this code it'll change but it's within the ballpark).
 
However, look at what happens when I include some kurtosis:
 
#same model as before
true.mod <- 'x1 ~~ 0.5*x2
             x1 ~~ 0.5*x3
             x2 ~~ 0.5*x3'

#same repetitions
reps <- 1000

#vectors to store sample skewnesses
x1s <- double(reps)
x2s <- double(reps)
x3s <- double(reps)
#vectors to store sample kurtoses
x1k <- double(reps)
x2k <- double(reps)
x3k <- double(reps)

#simulation loop
for (i in 1:reps) {
datum <- simulateData(true.mod, sample.nobs=1000, skewness=c(3,3,3), kurtosis=c(3,3,3))

x1s[i] <- describe(datum)$skew[1]
x2s[i] <- describe(datum)$skew[2]
x3s[i] <- describe(datum)$skew[3]
x1k <- describe(datum)$kurtosis[1]
x2k <- describe(datum)$kurtosis[2]
x3k <- describe(datum)$kurtosis[3]

}


#should be close to 3
> mean(x1s)
[1] 1.600354
> mean(x2s)
[1] 1.602386
> mean(x3s)
[1] 1.592869


#shold be close to 3
> mean(x1k)
[1] 2.96485
> mean(x2k)
[1] 2.366576
> mean(x3k)
[1] 1.747734
>



The skewness is almost half of what it should be! And only one estimate of sample kurtosis (x1) is somewhat closer to  its true population value of 3! Why? Is this beacuse of how lavaan implements ValeMaurelli1983() or is this a drawback of the method itself?
 
Thanks!
 
-Oscar

> skewness = skewness, :

That is just a silly bug in lavaan. Fixed now.

> *The skewness is almost half of what it should be! And only one estimate

> of sample kurtosis (x1) is somewhat closer to its true population value
> of 3! Why? Is this beacuse of how lavaan implements ValeMaurelli1983()

> or is this a drawback of the method itself?*

I think this is a drawback of the method itself (unless of course, I did
not implement it correctly)

It is relatively easy to retain skew/kurtosis for a single variable. But
the Vale-Maurelli method also tries to retain the correlation structure
among a set of variables. Obviously, there is trade-off there...

But I will try to double-check this anyway.

Yves.

messages.author: 373e56ec89625c50
messages.subject: Re: questions on how to implement simulateData()
parts:
I think this is a drawback of the method itself (unless of course, I did
not implement it correctly)

It is relatively easy to retain skew/kurtosis for a single variable. But
the Vale-Maurelli method also tries to retain the correlation structure
among a set of variables. Obviously, there is trade-off there...

I think you are correct in saying this is more of a thing of the method rather than its implementation. Apparently, the inequality
 
kurtosis > or = skewness^2-2 
 
must be satisfied for the method to work. It seems like if it is not, one may end up with biased estimates.

On 01/10/2014 10:52 AM, oolve...@gmail.com wrote:
> I think this is a drawback of the method itself (unless of course, I
> did
> not implement it correctly)
>
> It is relatively easy to retain skew/kurtosis for a single variable.
> But
> the Vale-Maurelli method also tries to retain the correlation structure
> among a set of variables. Obviously, there is trade-off there...
>
> I think you are correct in saying this is more of a thing of the method
> rather than its implementation. Apparently, the inequality
> kurtosis > or = skewness^2-2
> must be satisfied for the method to work. It seems like if it is
> not, one may end up with biased estimates.

True. The original paper of Fleishman (1978) has a nice figure (page
527) illustrating the combination of values for skewness/kurtosis for
which the method is valid. The way I implemented this in lavaan is that
if the values fall outside this range, we aim to get the best possible
solution anyway, but this will deviate from the target values. Perhaps a
warning should be in order?

Yves.

That is probably a good idea. We can always use extra warnings every now and then :-)
 
On a related note, the Vale & Maurelli implementation requires the estimation of what they call an "intermediate correlation matrix".
 
Is it possible to extract said "intermediate correlation matrix" from somewhere in simulateData() function? I assume it must be stored somewhere during the data-generation procedure because it is needed (alongside with Fleishman's method) to get back the covariance matrix intended for the population.
 
Thanks!
 
- Oscar
